questions.text:
The simplified SOP (Sum of Product) from the Boolean expression
[latex](P + \bar{Q} + \bar{R}) . (P + {Q} + R) . (P + Q +\bar{R})[/latex]
is
questions.solution:
Each factor is a maxterm with P = 0 that makes F = 0: (Q, R) = (1, 1), (0, 0), (0, 1). So for P = 0, F = 1 only when Q = 1, R = 0; for P = 1, F = 1 always.

[latex]F=P+Q\bar R[/latex]

Answer: [latex]P+Q.\bar R[/latex]

questions.text: The Excess-3 code is also called
questions.solution:
In Excess-3, the code of 9 [latex]-[/latex] d is the bitwise complement of the code of d (e.g. 2 = 0101, 7 = 1010). That is why it is called self-complementing.

Answer: Self-Complementing Code

questions.text: If [latex](12A7C)_{16} = (X)_8[/latex] then the value of X is
questions.solution:
Write in binary (4 bits per hex digit): 1 2 A 7 C = 0001 0010 1010 0111 1100.
Regroup in 3s from the right: 010 010 101 001 111 100 = 2 2 5 1 7 4.

Answer: 225174

questions.text: The circuit given in the figure below is
questions.solution:
Three inverters in a loop (an odd number) can never settle: whatever the output is, after three gate delays it comes back inverted. So the output keeps toggling: a ring oscillator producing a square wave with period 6 gate delays.

Answer: An oscillating circuit and its output is square wave

questions.text: The logic circuit given below converts a binary code y1, y2, y3 into
questions.solution:
The outputs are [latex]x_1=y_1[/latex], [latex]x_2=y_1\oplus y_2[/latex], [latex]x_3=x_2\oplus y_3[/latex]. Keeping the MSB and building the rest with XORs of neighbouring bits is the binary-Gray conversion; the key's answer is Gray code.

Answer: Gray code
